display.purpose: Hero headline only. Stacked block lines, sentence case, one optional italic word with a hand-drawn Thai Red underline.

headline.purpose: Section titles. Tighter tracking than the hero so it reads a rank below.

title.purpose: Book titles in product cards. Text serif, not display — the cover is the star.

body.purpose: Lead paragraphs and running copy at 72% ink, capped at 54ch.

label.purpose: The only uppercase role. Cover captions, badge text, credibility details.

shadows.name: shelf-rest
shadows.purpose: A book cover at rest in the grid, lit from upper-left.

shadows.name: shelf-lift
shadows.purpose: The same cover on hover, paired with translateY(-5px) and rotation to 0.

shadows.name: hero-slab
shadows.purpose: The larger, softer shadow beneath the two oversized hero book boards.

shadows.name: inner-board
shadows.purpose: The printed cover image inside a hero book board, giving the board real front thickness.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: The only easing in the system.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Fills, colors, and gap shifts on buttons and links.

narrative.overview:
A sunlit independent bookshop, mid-morning. Warm ivory paper everywhere, hairline ink rules dividing the space into calm compartments, and books tilted as if a person just set them down. Nothing on the page pretends to be a card, a panel, or a dashboard. The page is paper; the books are objects resting on it. That single distinction governs every visual decision in the system.

The system is deliberately quiet so that two things can be loud: the book covers, and the stepped color ladder. Covers are the largest elements on any screen and the only source of photographic color. The ladder — five bars climbing from deep plum to gold — is the one place the brand raises its voice, and it is rationed to the bottom of the hero and a single corner anchor per major section. Everything between them is ivory, ink, and thin lines.

Type carries the cultured, editorial register: a high-contrast serif for display, a workhorse text serif for everything readable. There is no sans-serif in the system, no uppercase headline, and no decorative religious ornament. The spiritual character comes from the books themselves, from generous air, and from restraint. The confirmed anti-references are: generic corporate publisher, crowded marketplace, luxury or exclusive boutique, and anything old-fashioned.
keyCharacteristics: Warm ivory ground (#fbf7ed) with a fine multiply-blended paper grain over the whole viewport
Hairline ink rules (1px #24231f) as the only structural divider — no card backgrounds, no borders on containers
Zero corner radius on every rectangle; circles reserved exclusively for icon controls
Book covers tilted 2–7°, straightening on hover
The stepped plum-to-gold ladder as the single signature graphic
Two serifs, no sans-serif, no uppercase headlines

rules.name: The Ladder-Is-One-Object Rule
rules.body: The five ladder colors are a single graphic, not a palette. Never pull one step out to color a button, a heading, a link, or an icon. If a design needs the ladder, it uses all five bars in sequence.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Thai Red is the only color that may carry interface meaning, and it appears on well under 10% of any screen. Its rarity is what makes it read as the brand.

rules.name: The Paper-Only Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one background color in the system. A section that wants separation earns it with a rule, whitespace, or the ladder — never with a tinted panel.

rules.name: The No-Sans Rule
rules.body: There is no sans-serif in this system. If something feels like it needs a sans, it needs a smaller serif at a wider tracking.

rules.name: The Headline-Stays-Cased Rule
rules.body: Display and Headline are always sentence case. Uppercase belongs to the Label role and nowhere else.

rules.name: The Numeral-As-Image Rule
rules.body: Large standalone figures are set in the display serif at a size where they read as a graphic element, paired with an uppercase label behind a 1px vertical rule.

rules.name: The Reduce-Decoration-First Rule
rules.body: When width runs out, decorative elements shrink or leave before product information does. Covers, titles, prices, and availability are the last things to change.

rules.name: The Flat-Page Rule
rules.body: Shadows attach to books only. A shadow on a button, a card, a header, a badge, or a section is a defect in this system.

rules.name: The Warm-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are warm brown (rgb(47 35 16 / …)), never neutral black. Black shadows on ivory read as dirt.

rules.name: The Zero-Radius Rule
rules.body: Rectangles never round. If a shape wants softening, it becomes a circle or it stays sharp.

dos: Do put every section on the same ivory paper (#fbf7ed) and separate them with rules and whitespace.
Do draw structure with 1px hairlines in Rule Ink (#24231f), leaving the outer edges of a grid open.
Do keep every rectangle at zero radius; use 50% circles only for icon controls.
Do tilt book covers 2–7° at rest and straighten them on hover with a 5px lift.
Do use warm brown shadows (rgb(47 35 16 / …)) and attach them only to books.
Do reserve uppercase for the Label role at 0.08–0.14em tracking.
Do hold transitions to 0.2–0.28s ease on at most two properties.
Do let the Dek sit tight (9px) under its headline so the pair reads as one unit.
Do shrink or drop decoration before touching product information on small screens.
donts: Don't introduce a second background color, a tinted panel, or a filled card.
Don't put a shadow on anything that is not a book.
Don't pull a single step out of the ladder to color a button, link, heading, or icon.
Don't add a sans-serif, or set a Display or Headline in uppercase.
Don't add entrance animations, parallax, or scroll-triggered motion.
Don't add decorative religious ornament — lotuses, mandalas, om marks, halos. The books carry the spiritual character.
Don't label the English cover assets in assets/books/ as Thai editions.
